## Problem

assertion-free on a security-critical path. `TestSudoCommandSelection` is titled to verify that the correct commands get the `sudo` prefix, but the match result is only logged, never asserted.

## Evidence

fail2ban/fail2ban_integration_sudo_test.go:221-233:
```go
calls := mockRunner.GetCalls()
found := slices.Contains(calls, tt.expectedCommand)
if !found && len(calls) > 0 {
    t.Logf("Expected command: %s", tt.expectedCommand)
    t.Logf("Actual calls: %v", calls)
}
if err != nil {
    t.Logf("Command execution failed (expected in test): %v", err)
}
```
There is no `t.Error`/`t.Fatal` in the loop body, so `found==false` cannot fail the test. Additionally the subject is `mockRunner.CombinedOutputWithSudo` (fail2ban.go:243) — a hand-written reimplementation of the production `OSRunner.CombinedOutputWithSudoContext` (fail2ban.go:72) — so even a real assertion would verify the mock's own reconstruction, not the production sudo-prefix wiring. (`RequiresSudo` itself is separately and correctly covered by TestRequiresSudo.)

## Impact

A regression that put `sudo` on a read-only command, or dropped it from a privileged one, passes green. The test advertises coverage of the escalation decision that it does not provide.

## Fix

Assert the match: `if !found { t.Errorf("expected command %q in calls %v", tt.expectedCommand, calls) }`. Separately, add a test that exercises the production decision — inject a fake exec/probe so `OSRunner.CombinedOutputWithSudoContext` runs its `RequiresSudo && HasSudoPrivileges` branch and records the `sudo`-prefixed argv, without shelling out to real sudo.

## Resolution
Replaced the t.Logf-only mismatch handling with t.Errorf so TestSudoCommandSelection now fails when the runner does not receive the expected (sudo-prefixed or bare) command. Proven failing-capable by perturbing the expected command. Residual noted in finding: the assertion still runs against MockRunner's reimplementation; exercising production OSRunner.CombinedOutputWithSudoContext end-to-end needs exec injection it does not currently expose (out of tests-only scope).
title: TestSudoCommandSelection cannot fail — sudo-escalation decision unasserted

## Problem

tautological + sleep-coordinated. The cancellation test asserts a condition the happy path always satisfies, so cancellation itself is never verified.

## Evidence

fail2ban/fail2ban_parallel_processing_test.go:131:
```go

    t.Error("Expected either completed or canceled results")
```

With 10 non-error items, every result is completed or canceled, so `completed+cancelled` is effectively always > 0. Cancel timing is nudged by a `time.Sleep` (line 93).

A worker pool that ignored context cancellation entirely (never cancelling anything) still passes. The test provides no evidence cancellation works.

Cancel deterministically (cancel the context before/while a known-blocking item runs), then assert `cancelledCount > 0` and that cancelled results carry `context.Canceled`. Remove the sleep-based coordination.

## Problem

flaky-pattern (test-order dependence). Several tests install a mock into the process-global runner with no defer/restore, while the package already provides `WithTestRunner` (test_helpers.go:268) for exactly this.

## Evidence

fail2ban/fail2ban_banned_context_test.go:23 (and the other 3 tests in the file):
```go
mock := setupMockForBannedInTest("192.168.1.100", `["sshd"]`)
SetRunner(mock)
client, err := NewClient("/var/log", "/etc/fail2ban/filter.d")
```
No `defer SetRunner(original)`. The same leak appears across the 3 tests in client_context_timeout_test.go.

## Impact

Whichever test runs last leaves its mock installed; a later test that reads the global runner sees contaminated state. Order-dependent failures are the kind teams learn to ignore.

Wrap these with the existing `WithTestRunner(t, mock, func(){ ... })` helper (or add `t.Cleanup(func(){ SetRunner(original) })`) so global state is always restored.

Replaced 7 bare SetRunner(mock) calls (4 in fail2ban_banned_context_test.go, 3 in client_context_timeout_test.go) with t.Cleanup(WithTestRunner(t, mock)), which sets the runner and registers automatic restoration of the original global runner. Eliminates the test-order dependence / cross-test contamination. All affected tests pass.

## Problem

The local `golangci-lint` hook hard-codes its version in `entry:` (`go run .../golangci-lint@v2.13.2 run`). No Renovate manager reads an `entry:` string, so this pin never moves; the same linter is pinned at v2.15.0 in the Makefile and v2.14.0 in both workflows. Class: manifest drift (one tool, three versions, four sites).

## Evidence

Manifest: `.pre-commit-config.yaml:34` `entry: go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.13.2 run`; `Makefile:14` `GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION := v2.15.0`; `.github/workflows/lint.yml:38` and `pr-lint.yml:49` `version: v2.14.0`.
Lock leg: none — `go run module@version` resolves through the module proxy + sumdb; no lockfile applies.
Usage: the hook runs in the `prek` CI job (`pr-lint.yml:86-93`).
Renovate Dependency Dashboard (issue #1) lists the Makefile and both workflow pins but not the hook pin — the hook is invisible to Renovate.
Failing scenario, observed: Renovate PR #235 (go toolchain 1.27.1 → 1.27.3 [security], open since 2026-10-10) fails `prek` with `could not load export data: internal error in importing "internal/goarch" (cannot decode "internal/goarch", export data version 5 is greater than maximum supported version 4)` from golangci-lint v2.13.2 (run 40521990806, job 122251249202). The `PR Lint` job, using v2.14.0, passes on the same commit.

## Impact

A security toolchain update has been blocked for 17 days by a linter pin nobody is told about. Every future Go release whose export-data format changes repeats this, and the hook silently disagrees with the other three pins in the meantime.

## Fix

Remove the duplicated pin instead of syncing it: make the hook call the Makefile target that already carries the Renovate-tracked `GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION`, e.g. `entry: make lint-go`. One version site for local+prek runs; Renovate keeps it current through the Makefile custom manager.

## Resolution
Local golangci-lint hook now runs `make lint-go`, so Makefile GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION (Renovate-tracked, v2.15.0) is the single local/prek pin; workflows bumped to v2.15.0. make lint-go: 0 issues under go1.27.3.
title: Untracked golangci-lint pin in the local pre-commit hook blocks the go1.27.3 security update

## Problem

All four `OSRunner` exec sites use `exec.CommandContext(...).CombinedOutput()` with the default Cancel (SIGKILL to the direct child) and `WaitDelay == 0`. sudo cannot relay SIGKILL. Without a pty, the command sudo started keeps the output pipe open, and `CombinedOutput` waits for EOF until that orphan exits.

## Evidence

`fail2ban/fail2ban.go:64`, `:82`, `:90` (`exec.CommandContext(ctx, constants.SudoCommand, sudoArgs...).CombinedOutput()`), `:94`; production sets `Cmd.Cancel`/`WaitDelay` nowhere. Measured by two subagents with `sh -c "sleep 3; :"` standing in for sudo: a 200ms context returned after 3s; with `WaitDelay` set it returned after 500-700ms. os/exec docs: with WaitDelay zero, pipes are read until EOF, "which might not occur until orphaned subprocesses ... have also closed their descriptors".

## Impact

CommandTimeout, ParallelTimeout and FileTimeout do not bound f2b when fail2ban-client or fail2ban-regex hangs; the orphan keeps running after f2b gives up.

## Fix

Route the four sites through one helper that sets `cmd.Cancel = func() error { return cmd.Process.Signal(syscall.SIGTERM) }` (sudo relays SIGTERM) and `cmd.WaitDelay = constants.CommandWaitDelay` (new constant, 5s), then `return cmd.CombinedOutput()`.

## Resolution
All four OSRunner exec sites go through runCombined: Cancel sends SIGTERM (relayed by sudo) and WaitDelay (5s) stops waiting on orphan-held pipes. TestRunCombinedBoundsOrphanedChild returns in 0.4s; the no-WaitDelay mutant blocks 30s and fails.
title: Context timeouts do not bound sudo-wrapped commands: SIGKILL hits only sudo and no WaitDelay is set

## Problem

`f2b test-filter <name>` runs `sudo fail2ban-regex <logpath> <filter.conf>`. The logpath comes from a user-controllable filter file and is checked only against the log allowlist, which contains whole subtrees `/home`, `/opt` and `/usr/local`. The filter allowlist also contains `/home`. Under the documented `sudo f2b` deployment, a confined operator can make fail2ban-regex read any file under those trees as root and print its lines.

## Evidence

`fail2ban/pathsecurity.go:24` `paths := []string{"/var/log", "/opt", "/usr/local", "/home"}`; `:31` `paths := []string{"/etc/fail2ban", "/usr/local/etc/fail2ban", "/opt/fail2ban", "/home"}`; `fail2ban/fail2ban.go:565` validates logpath with `CreateLogPathConfig()`, then `:572-573` runs `CombinedOutputWithSudoContext(ctx, constants.Fail2BanRegexCommand, validatedLogPath, cleanPath)`; `sudo.go:137-139` makes fail2ban-regex always sudo. A recording-runner PoC got a `/home` logpath accepted (`/etc/shadow` was rejected). Real fail2ban-regex 1.0.2 prints non-matching lines under "Missed line(s)". Scenario: `sudo f2b --filter-dir /home/me/f test-filter leak` with `logpath = /home/victim/.ssh/id_rsa`.

## Impact

Under restricted sudo for f2b, a user reads other users' and root-only files (SSH keys, app secrets) as root. The NIT-106 logpath fix relies on an allowlist too broad to contain this.

## Fix

Narrow `GetLogAllowedPaths` to `{"/var/log"}` and `GetFilterAllowedPaths` to `{"/etc/fail2ban", "/usr/local/etc/fail2ban", "/opt/fail2ban"}`, keeping the `ALLOW_DEV_PATHS` gate. Update docs and tests that rely on `/home`, `/opt` or `/usr/local`.

## Resolution
GetLogAllowedPaths narrowed to /var/log and GetFilterAllowedPaths to /etc/fail2ban, /usr/local/etc/fail2ban, /opt/fail2ban (ALLOW_DEV_PATHS gate kept). TestNewClientPathTraversalProtection updated to the approved policy with rejection cases for /opt and /home log dirs and a /home filter dir; full suite passes.
title: test-filter is a read-as-root primitive over /home, /opt, /usr/local and /var/log

## Problem

License lens, missing attribution. Every f2b binary statically links `github.com/spf13/cobra` (Apache-2.0) and `github.com/spf13/pflag` (BSD-3-Clause). BSD-3-Clause clause 2 requires binary redistributions to reproduce the copyright notice and license in the accompanying materials, and Apache-2.0 §4(a) requires giving recipients a copy of the license. The archives (`files:` LICENSE.md, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/*), the nfpm packages (`contents:` LICENSE.md, README.md) and the Docker image contain only the project's own MIT license.

## Evidence

`go version -m` on linux and darwin builds → `dep github.com/spf13/cobra v1.10.2`, `dep github.com/spf13/pflag v1.0.10` (mousetrap is Windows-only and not linked; no Windows builds). `go-licenses report .` → `cobra ... Apache-2.0`, `pflag ... BSD-3-Clause`, `f2b ... MIT`. `.goreleaser.yaml:233-237` archive `files:`; `.goreleaser.yaml:357-361` nfpm `contents:`; `Dockerfile` copies only the binary.

## Impact

The first release would distribute third-party code without the notices its licenses require. Licenses are compatible with MIT; only attribution is missing.

## Fix

Generate notices at release time with the ecosystem tool instead of a hand-maintained file: add a Renovate-tracked `GO_LICENSES_VERSION` and a `licenses` target to the Makefile (`go run github.com/google/go-licenses/v2@$(GO_LICENSES_VERSION) save . --save_path=third_party/licenses --force`), make it goreleaser's `before` hook (replacing the no-op `go generate`), gitignore `/third_party/`, and ship `third_party/licenses` in archives, nfpm packages and the Docker image.

## Resolution
Correction to Evidence: .goreleaser.yaml does have a f2b-windows build, so mousetrap (Apache-2.0) IS linked into Windows binaries. Fix: scripts/collect-licenses.sh (goreleaser before hook, replacing the no-op go generate) collects license files of every third-party module over the union of all GOOS (go list -deps; go-licenses rejected: it cannot load a foreign GOOS) into gitignored third_party/licenses; archives (third_party/licenses/**/*), nfpm (/usr/share/doc/f2b/licenses tree) and the image (/usr/share/licenses/f2b via dockers_v2 extra_files) ship them. Verified by snapshot release: tar.gz and .deb contain cobra/pflag/mousetrap licenses; amd64 image lists them.

## Problem

The shared preset (`github>ivuorinen/renovate-config`) already (a) defines the Makefile `# renovate:` custom manager and (b) groups every source of one tool into one PR (`golangci-lint`, `goreleaser`, ... groups, rules 29-48) precisely because "Renovate opened one PR per source and the pins drifted apart". The repo config re-declares the Makefile custom manager (a duplicate extractor) and appends a `custom.regex` + `Makefile` packageRule setting `groupName: "development tools"`. Repo rules apply after preset rules, so that groupName overrides the per-tool groups for every Makefile pin and re-splits each tool across PRs.

## Evidence

`.github/renovate.json:8-19` Makefile customManager (same regex shape as the preset's own Makefile manager); `.github/renovate.json:32-45` packageRule `matchManagers: ["custom.regex"], matchFileNames: ["Makefile", "**/*.mk"], groupName: "development tools"`.
Observed drift right now: goreleaser `Makefile:12` v2.18.3 vs `release.yml:67,81` v2.18.2; prek `Makefile:39` v0.5.5 vs `pr-lint.yml:93` v0.5.7; golangci-lint `Makefile:14` v2.15.0 vs workflows v2.14.0.
Dependency Dashboard: the goreleaser workflow pins are in PR #247 (`goreleaser` group) while the Makefile goreleaser pin sits in the separate `renovate/development-tools` branch with gosec/prek/markdownlint-cli2.

## Impact

Each tool upgrade lands as two independently merged PRs, so local `make` targets and CI run different versions of the same linter/releaser between merges. That is the exact skew that made golangci-lint panic on Go 1.27 in 8cac473.

## Fix

Delete the duplicate Makefile customManager and the local `development tools` packageRule from `.github/renovate.json`; the preset already supplies both, and its per-tool groups then apply to Makefile pins too. Keep only the `release.yml` `version:` customManager, which the preset does not cover. Validate with `npx --yes --package renovate -- renovate-config-validator .github/renovate.json`.

## Resolution
renovate.json reduced to `extends` only: the local packageRule (which overrode the preset's per-tool groups for Makefile pins) is gone; both local customManagers were dead (bare `^...$` managerFilePatterns are globs in Renovate and matched nothing; the preset supplies the Makefile manager and the github-actions manager updates goreleaser-action `version:` natively, as PR #247 shows); minimumReleaseAge duplicated the preset. Dead `# renovate:` comments removed from release.yml. renovate-config-validator: validated successfully.
title: Local renovate.json overrides the preset's per-tool groups, so Makefile and workflow pins of one tool drift apart

## Problem

loop-invariant-work. `collectLogLines` reads (and decompresses) each rotated file completely before the current log, keeping only the newest MaxLines after the fact. Reading never stops early, and logs-watch re-reads unchanged rotated files on every tick.

## Evidence

`fail2ban/logs.go:128` `// Rotated logs are read oldest-first, then the current log last.`; `:129-133` loop over `rotated` calling `readAndAppend`; `:184` `fileConfig.MaxLines = 0`. logs-watch poll: `cmd/logswatch.go:101-108` ticker → `pollOnce` → `GetLogLinesWithLimitContext` → `collectLogLines`. Measured: 20k-line current log plus 4 gzip rotated logs of 250k lines each took 318ms per call (493ms with jail=sshd) vs 1.4ms/5.5ms for the current log alone, same 1000 lines returned.

## Impact

Cost grows linearly with log retention on every `f2b logs` call and every logs-watch poll. Past FileTimeout (10s, about 20M lines), every read fails with deadline exceeded and logs-watch never prints new lines.

## Fix

Read newest first (current log, then rotated in reverse), stop once MaxLines matching lines are collected, then reassemble chunks oldest-to-newest and keep the last MaxLines. The output is identical (newest MaxLines, chronological).

## Resolution
Logs are read newest first (current, then rotated newest to oldest), stop at MaxLines and are reassembled chronologically. Verified: mutation of the MaxLines stop killed by TestCollectLogLinesStopsOnceCurrentLogSuffices; order pinned by TestCollectLogLinesNewestFirstAcrossRotatedLogs.

## Problem

unsafe-publication. The goroutine is parked in `<-sigCh`, so os/signal hands a late signal directly to it and the deferred drain finds the buffer empty. Execute returns and main reads `SignalExitCode()` before the goroutine's `Store`. `close(sigCh)` after a concurrent `signal.Stop` can also panic with "send on closed channel".

## Evidence

`cmd/root.go:97-110` deferred `signal.Stop(sigCh)` / non-blocking drain / `close(sigCh)`; `:111-121` goroutine `sig, ok := <-sigCh` ... `interruptCode.Store(...)`; nothing joins it. A scratch replica raising the signal at completion: 8-67 of 16-144 delivered signals per run were read as 0; a joined version lost 0 across 12x5000 iterations.

## Impact

Ctrl-C/SIGTERM landing as a command finishes exits 0 or 1 instead of 130/143, the case NIT-70 was marked fixed for.

## Fix

Never close sigCh; add `stop`/`done` channels: goroutine `defer close(done); select { case sig := <-sigCh: store; signal.Stop; cancel(); case <-stop: }`; defer: `signal.Stop(sigCh); close(stop); <-done;` then drain sigCh non-blockingly and store if present.

## Resolution
watchSignals' stop joins the goroutine, then drains sigCh; sigCh is never closed. Verified: mutation dropping <-done killed by TestWatchSignalsRecordsSignalBeforeStopReturns; passes under -race.
title: Signal goroutine is never joined, so a signal at command completion still exits 0/1 about half the time (NIT-70 incomplete)

## Problem

`cmd.Logger` writes slog text while `ContextualLogger` writes JSON, and both go to the same writer (stderr or `--log-file`).

## Evidence

`cmd/logging.go:22-37` constructs the contextual logger with the JSON handler; `cmd.Logger` uses `SlogText`. Both are redirected by `Logger.SetOutput(f)` (`cmd/root.go:201`).

## Impact

A log shipper must parse two formats from one stream; a JSON-only parser drops the text lines.

## Fix

Use one format for both (JSON when `--log-file` is set, text otherwise), chosen in one place.

## Resolution
NewContextualLogger shares cmd.Logger's *SlogLogger (syncContextualLogger deleted); PersistentPreRunE picks JSON for --log-file and text otherwise. docs/security.md and docs/faq.md now state that (they claimed JSON on stderr). Verified: mutation killed by TestLogFormatChosenOnce.
title: Two log formats interleave on one sink: text Logger and JSON ContextualLogger
